answer_summary: Khanani says the 5-year Portal subgroup supports sustained ranibizumab delivery with stable vision and anatomy in previously treated nAMD patients. He emphasizes that about 95% did not need supplemental treatment between refill exchanges and that long-term safety appeared manageable, with no endophthalmitis in the long-followed subgroup.

answer_summary: Khanani highlights durability as the key faricimab finding: more patients reached 16-week dosing while maintaining comparable vision and anatomy versus q8w aflibercept. He links durability to real-world vision preservation because undertreatment harms outcomes, and says ongoing controlled and real-world data, including AVONELLE-X and TRUCKEE, should clarify safety, switch response, and durability; he also calls for broader minority enrollment in trials.

answer_summary: Khanani organizes the exudative AMD pipeline by development stage: OPT-302 as a phase 3 attempt to improve vision beyond VEGF-A blockade, subretinal RGX-314 as sustained anti-VEGF delivery to reduce burden and potentially improve anatomy, intravitreal gene therapies, and TKI implants or suspensions. His main theme is that emerging therapies should either improve visual outcomes or reduce treatment frequency while maintaining disease control.
answer_basis: Ophthalmology Times Europe / Modern Retina edited transcript, EURETINA 2023: Emerging therapies for exudative AMD, https://europe.ophthalmologytimes.com/view/euretina-2023-emerging-therapies-for-exudative-amd

answer_summary: Khanani calls AAVIATE important because it was the first suprachoroidal gene-therapy trial and showed early tolerability plus meaningful reduction in treatment burden, over 70%, while maintaining anatomy and vision at 6 months in the first two dose levels. He stresses that RGX-314 is not curative, but a one-time in-clinic approach could reduce repeated anti-VEGF injections; higher-dose and neutralizing-antibody analyses were still ongoing.
answer_basis: HCPLive article quotes, Gene Therapy RGX-314 Benefits nAMD Treatment Burden in Phase 2 AAVIATE, https://www.hcplive.com/view/gene-therapy-rgx-314-benefits-namd-treatment-burden-phase-2-aaviate
answer_limitations: Article contains selected quotes and reporter summary, not a full transcript. Early phase 2 data with short follow-up at the time.

answer_summary: Khanani describes fellow-eye bilateral ABBV-RGX-314 data as a milestone because nAMD is often bilateral. He emphasizes no new safety signals, no intraocular inflammation or serious drug-related events, sustained BCVA and CRT, similar protein production between eyes, and large burden reduction: 78% injection-free and 97% lower annualized anti-VEGF need at 9 months.
answer_basis: HCPLive article quotes and key takeaways, Arshad Khanani, MD: First Results from Fellow Eye Dosing of RGX-314 in nAMD, https://www.hcplive.com/view/arshad-khanani-md-first-results-from-fellow-eye-dosing-of-rgx-314-in-namd
answer_limitations: Article contains selected quotes and reported data, not a full transcript. Fellow-eye substudy was small and follow-up was 9 months.

answer_summary: Khanani explains RHONE-X as a 2-year open-label extension of YOSEMITE/RHINE in which prior arms rolled into faricimab treat-and-extend up to q16w.
